paragraphs: On Friday afternoon, Pat's class had a play on the school stage. Pat was a tiger. May and Lily came to watch, because Pat was May's brother. After the play, the hall was full of children in costumes. The hall was loud and very happy. "Where is Pat?" asked May.

Pat's teacher stood near the door. "Pat has just finished a big job," she said. "He wears an orange tiger costume with a black stripe on each arm." "He has a green paper necklace and a pocket on his costume." "He stands next to the stage steps, and he gives water to the other children." "Thank you," said May. "We look until we find him."

The first tiger stood by the door. He had a black stripe on each arm, but he had no necklace. He also ate a banana. "That is not Pat," said Lily. "He does not give water to anyone." Next, they saw a boy in a white doctor uniform. "He is not a tiger," said May. They also saw a girl in a blue bird costume.

A second tiger sat at a table with cups. He had a black stripe on each arm and a red necklace. "His necklace is red," said May. "Pat has a green one." Then Lily looked at the stage steps. "There!" she said. A third tiger stood there. He had a black stripe on each arm, a green necklace, and a pocket. He gave a cup of water to a small bird.

"Pat!" called May. Pat ran to her, and his tail went up and down. "Did you see me, May?" he asked. "I made the tiger sound three times!" "We saw you once, on the stage," said Lily. "You were a very good tiger." Pat took a small paper star from his pocket. "This is for you, May," he said. May put the star on her school uniform and smiled.
text.summary: After a school play, May and Lily look for May's little brother Pat in the hall full of costumes. A teacher gives them a short description, and they find the right tiger.
